sources.classification: labelled from the task code, 2026-10-10: a transformer language model trained from scratch, so `ai_training`; precision fp16 (autocast and gradient scaler); params counted from the layer shapes = 519 963 095 = embedding 274 160 640 (267 735 tokens x 1024, tied with the output weights) + output bias 267 735 + 18 layers x 13 640 704 + relative-position biases 2 048 (vocabulary 267 735: WikiText-103 training tokens and <eos>, not counted on the stand's machine); seq_len = target length (the memory adds 256 more positions of context); the run is bounded by max_step 400, not by epochs: epochs and dataset_samples are left out

measurements.source: Lambda, github.com/lambdal/deeplearning-benchmark, commit aa5addb6 (2025-12-17), pytorch/pytorch-train-throughput-fp16.csv, column transformerxllarge (training throughput, tokens/s), single-GPU rows run with batch 48 (pytorch/pytorch-train-bs-fp16.csv; config_pytorch_80GB.sh): 'A100 80GB SXM4' 17918; 'A100 80GB PCIe' 17082; 'H100 80GB PCIe Gen5' 22586, 'LambdaCloud H100 80GB PCIe Gen5' 21874; 'H100 80GB SXM5' 30841 (the five other H100 80GB SXM5 rows hold 0.0 and are left out)

measurements.compute_ratio_note: throughput[A100 80GB SXM4] / throughput[GPU]; the two H100 PCIe rows pooled by geometric mean (22227 tokens/s); H100 SXM5 is one host. The throughput is tokens / elapsed time per 10 steps, averaged over 400 steps after the first 3 values
